# AI Engineering Compiler v0.6.0

Everything a defended agent configuration needs already existed: deny rules,
the sandbox, accepted gaps, an audit. This release makes it one line.

## `security: hardened`

```yaml
# .ai/manifest.yaml or .ai/blueprint.yaml
security: hardened
```

On the next `aie sync`:

- **Secret files are denied.** The agent's file tools cannot read `.env`,
  `.env.*`, `*.pem`, or `*.key`, the same files `aie audit` checks for.
- **The sandbox is on**, so those rules also bind shell commands such as
  `cat .env`, and the sandbox's protected paths cover the agent's own
  configuration.

Your own `permissions` and `sandbox` blocks still apply on top, for example to
pre-allow the hosts your project needs. Deny still wins over allow, and setting
`sandbox.enabled: false` alongside the preset is an error rather than a silent
override. The preset expands at sync time, so a later release that improves it
reaches your workspace on the next sync; every change to it will be listed in
the changelog.

## `aie init --secure`

Starts a workspace with the preset. Codex cannot enforce it, and the generated
file says so and accepts the gap visibly, so the first sync passes `--strict`
and a manifest workspace audits clean. A blueprint workspace reports one
finding, `hook-no-ci-backstop`, until its commit hook's CI check is added to
the project's pipeline.

## `aie audit` points at the fix

The fixes for `deny-empty`, `sandbox-disabled`, and `secret-readable` now name
`security: hardened`.

## Limits

The preset covers four filename patterns. A secret stored under any other name
needs its own rule. See the
[threat model](https://github.com/akin-oz/ai-engineering/blob/v0.6.0/docs/threat-model.md).

## Upgrading

No action needed. Workspaces that do not name a preset compile exactly as in
0.5.1.
